name: Comparatives & Superlatives
moduleIntroduction: Welcome to the Comparatives & Superlatives module! This is how we compare things in English. In French, you almost always use 'Plus' (*plus grand, plus intelligent*). In English, we have two systems: adding a tail (-er) or using a helper (more). If you use the French logic for everything, you will make mistakes like 'more big' or 'the most small'.
contrastiveExplanation:
Short Adjectives (1 syllable):
English: Add -er (Bigger) or -est (Biggest).
French: Uses 'Plus' (Plus grand).

Long Adjectives (2+ syllables):
English: Use 'More' (More expensive) or 'The Most' (The most expensive).
French: Uses 'Plus' (Plus cher).

Connecting Words:
English: Better THAN me.
French: Meilleur QUE moi. (Beware: 'Que' usually means 'That', but here it means 'Than').

commonErrors.frenchConnection: Applying French logic ('plus' = 'more') to short words.
Applying French logic ('le plus' = 'the most') to short words.
Using both systems at once for emphasis.

items.questionText: This car is ___ better than the old one.
items.feedback: Correct! Use 'much' (or 'far') to emphasize a comparative. Never use 'more better'.

items.questionText: She is my ___ sister.

items.questionText: The situation went from bad to ___.
This is ___ expensive hotel in the city.
items.feedback: Correct! 'The least' is the superlative of 'less'.

items.questionText: He is ___ to me.
items.feedback: Correct! Latin comparatives (superior, inferior, senior) do not take -er or more.

items.questionText: This is by far ___ cake I have tasted.
items.feedback: Correct! 'By far' is used to emphasize superlatives.

items.questionText: The faster you run, ___ tired you get.
items.feedback: Correct! Double comparative: 'The faster..., the more...'

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Plus tu cours vite, plus tu es fatigué...
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The faster you run, the more tired you get...

items.questionText: She looks ___ older than her age.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Slightly' is a modifier for comparatives.

items.questionText: He is one of the ___ men in the world.
items.feedback: Correct! 'One of the' + Superlative + Plural Noun.

items.questionText: Can you go any ___?
items.feedback: Correct! 'Further' means 'more' (abstract). 'Farther' is physical distance (though often interchangeable). In this context (continue), 'further' is better.

items.questionText: It is not ___ warm as yesterday.
items.feedback: Correct! In negative comparisons, we can use 'not SO... as' instead of 'not AS... as'.

frenchComparison.whyDifficult: 'Not so... as' is a formal alternative to 'Not as... as'.

items.questionText: She is the ___ of the three girls.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Je préfère le café au thé...
